answer: An agent network can curb Sybil clones by binding each node to a discontinued smartcard whose factory certificate proves it is a retired silicon relic. When a beacon emits a challenge pulse, each node must return a signature within one signing interval so one chip cannot serve multiple agents. Since production has ended, attackers must buy scarce modules smaller than a walnut and dedicated readers per identity. However, adversaries can still hoard surplus units from e-waste markets.
